svg.title: 665B FIM: training examples and zero-shot readouts
svg.desc: An AR-only checkpoint is annealed with annotation-guided FIM. Evaluation fixes one template, then compares teacher-forced and all-candidate scores in forward and reverse-complement orientations.
svg.text: 665B FIM · from AR-only training to two-sided inference
Autoregressive (AR) training → fill-in-the-middle (FIM) annealing of the same causal MoE model.
No optimizer reset · no biological metadata
DNA training so far: AR only
What the model sees → what receives loss
Next-base loss across the DNA sequence
One fixed evaluation template; many training presentations
Shares are within FIM; distances not to scale.
Nearby gaps never overlap the landmark.
The entire target is absent from L and R.
Literal labels use text BPE; DNA uses one token per base.
8K eval budget: trim distant context ends to fit syntax + answer.
Eval keeps the form shown at left.
Two context presentations × two answer readouts
Base readouts normalize over lowercase a / c / g / t
AR · one flank per model pass
FIM · both flanks in each model pass
Choose either readout below for either context presentation above
Target atg · same per-strand TF rule as Evo2–20B
Each prediction receives earlier true answer bases.
RC example: cat. Align positions + complements;
combine forward / RC at each answer position.
Example k = 2: all 16 motifs, no selected path
Candidate prefixes only; no true answer supplied.
Fuse whole-motif probabilities; select the maximum.
× RC = equal-weight geometric combination, normalized again
Motifs: exact whole-answer accuracy. Conservation: observed-base probability → AUROC.
Core/non-core AUROC: TF uses mean true-base probability; All 4ᵏ uses whole-motif probability Q(y).
SV impact · standard forward-only AR scoring

Known sequences; no masking or generation.
The same ten observed boundary bases.
Each probability uses the actual prefix.
Higher score = lower support after deletion.
AR × RC rows reuse this SV score.
